name: CICIoV2024
description: The Internet of Vehicles (IoV) faces growing cybersecurity challenges as vehicles become more connected by networks, which requires efficient Anomaly Intrusion Detection Systems (AIDS). This paper uses CICIoV2024, a comprehensive modern dataset for IoV security research. Also reflects real-world attacks conducted on a Ford vehicle's Controller Area Network (CAN) bus system. The dataset covers popular attack scenarios, including Denial-of-Service (DoS) and spoofing (steering wheel, RPM, gas, and speed controls) attacks. We implemented a systematic machine learning pipeline to build AIDS based on a comprehensive dataset evaluation. The evaluation includes binary classification (Benign vs Attack), categorical classification (Benign, DoS, Spoofing), and multiclass classification (Benign, Steering Wheel Spoofing, Gas Spoofing, RPM Spoofing, Speed Spoofing) where the Logistic Regression, Random Forest, AdaBoost, and Deep Neural Networks are used in implementation.
